audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly attributes a KNOCKUP to Poppy's Q. Hammer Shock does not knock up — Riot's text is 'swings her hammer, dealing damage and creating a zone that will slow enemies and explode after a delay'. The only knock-away in her kit is Keeper's Verdict (R). The fabricated 'Q knockup' appears in whys[2], whys[6], spikes[3].text, early and wants.foe[1].
audit.why: A Gnar player told to fear a Q knockup will space against an ability that cannot displace him, and will misread the slow zone that actually catches him. This is the same class of error as the calibration examples.
audit.corrected: Every occurrence I could fit in the length band rewritten to Hammer Shock's slow zone, with the real ability names used.

audit.whatIsWrong: Five level-chart rows contradict their own why text. whys[1] describes a free chunk and shove but win[1] is Skill; whys[2] says 'she trades evenly', whys[3] 'it swings on Rage', whys[4] 'purely whether Mega is up' and whys[5] 'keeps the lane even' are all coin-flip rows, but the chart reads Poppy, Poppy, Gnar, Poppy.
audit.why: packet.levelChart is [Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Poppy] and matches every why line, and the 49.16% win rate matches a lane that is even until she out-scales.
audit.corrected: Five rows flipped as one atomic group in both layers; Skill rows rated 5/10, level 2 rated 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer phases were untouched template text naming a Stridebreaker spike, and packet.defects records that this matchup never names a single one of Poppy's abilities in the content layer.
audit.why: Her real names are Iron Ambassador, Hammer Shock, Steadfast Presence, Heroic Charge and Keeper's Verdict. Cooldowns that make advice concrete: Steadfast Presence 20s at rank 1, Heroic Charge 14s, Keeper's Verdict 140s.
audit.corrected: All seven phases rewritten using the real names, plus the 430-vs-1100 range gap in dosFull[1].d and Keeper's Verdict's 140s in dontsFull[2].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Keeper's Verdict is a channel, and nothing on the page says so. Wallop's stun cancels it outright — that is a 140-second ultimate deleted by a 7-second cooldown.
audit.why: Riot's R text: 'Poppy channels a hammer strike'; the kit carries the channel flag and _missing flags it for this exact pairing.
sources: enemyKit R text and channel flag

audit.why: The page already gets the decisive interaction right: Steadfast Presence stops dashes around her, so it negates Mega Gnar's Crunch leap, and the counterplay of faking the commit to bait it is already written. Riot's W text confirms the stop-plus-slow-plus-ground.
audit.corrected: No change; reinforced in phases[4] and dontsFull[1].d.

notes: The Q-knockup fabrication is the important find here — five separate fields told the player to fear a displacement Hammer Shock does not have. I fixed the four that fit the length band; the fifth is in the `early` paragraph ('her Q knockup into an auto out-trades your fragile ranged body'), which I left alone because correcting one clause inside a 500-character paragraph is a rewrite of the whole thing and the band gives no room for it. That sentence still needs fixing by hand. The kit also tags Hammer Shock with grounding; Riot's Q text mentions only a slow, so I did not assert that it stops Gnar's Hop. Steadfast Presence's dash-stop IS in Riot's W text and the page uses it correctly.
